incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 through L.223-56 and R.223-1 through R.223-29 (formation, share capital, management of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Civil Code Articles 1835 to 1844-17 (general contract-of-partnership rules); Decree No. 67-237 of 23 March 1967 on commercial companies; applicable sections of the Environmental Code (ICPE regime) and Public Health Code (alcohol wholesale licensing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; all applications must be filed electronically through the single national portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 – Demande unique d'immatriculation (Single Registration Application) filed together with the signed articles of association (Statuts), the capital deposit certificate, and the certificate of publication of the legal notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital (a SARL may be formed with as little as €1). If the subscribed cash capital is €5,000 or less, it must be fully paid up before filing and held in a blocked escrow account with a French bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; if it exceeds €5,000, at least 20% must be released on incorporation and the balance within five years. In-kind contributions must be fully transferred at formation, and a contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports) is required unless all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment. Escrowed funds are released to the Manager only upon presentation of the K-bis registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST CORPORATE RESOLUTION OF THE CONSTITUENT SHAREHOLDERS

The founders unanimously resolve:

1. The articles of association are approved, and the Company is constituted as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée.
2. The share capital of €[•], divided into [number] shares, is subscribed in full and acknowledged as paid up per the deposit certificate.
3. The registered office is established at [address], France.
4. [Manager] is appointed as sole Manager (Gérant), with the powers and term set out in the articles.
5. The Manager is authorized to execute and file all incorporation instruments and disclosure formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, signing and adoption of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Constitutive shareholders' meeting (private signature sous seing privé) or a notary where real-property contributions or specific validations are required; professional counsel certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene all founding shareholders or their duly authorized proxies and adopt the final Statuts. The Statuts must state the corporate form (SARL), corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (including craft beer production, cold-chain wholesale, storage, and export of fermented malt beverages), share capital, share classes and rights, management powers, auditor appointment, and corporate duration (maximum 99 years). Every shareholder signs each page and the final signature page. Where contributions in kind are made, annex the commissaire aux apports report unless unanimously waived, and attach the inventory of in-kind contributions.
required_dossiers: Original articles of association signed by all shareholders
Report of the contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports) or unanimous waiver
Identity documents of all founding shareholders
Declaration of non-conviction of the designated Manager (déclaration de non-condamnation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry flags a statutory defect, execute a corrective amending resolution signed by all shareholders and re-submit the corrected Statuts; if a notary's legalization is required, the notary will issue a supplementary deed before the registry deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of the subscribed capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC); Banque de France intervention for refusal of a bank account (right to an account).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company being formed and deposit the full cash subscription, or the statutory minimum fraction where capital exceeds €5,000. The depositary financial institution issues the capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) together with a release undertaking stating that funds will be released solely to the Manager upon presentation of the K-bis extract and a board authorization for disbursement.
required_dossiers: Cash subscription declarations (bulletin de souscription) executed by each shareholder
Proof of wire transfer or deposit instrument
Copy of the draft articles of association
Original capital deposit certificate issued by the bank or CDC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the credit institution refuses to open the account, file a request with the Banque de France under the droit au compte procedure, which designates a bank within one to three business days; the deposit certificate is then issued by the designated institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice in a legal gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) approved by the Prefecture of the department where the registered office is situated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the selected JAL to publish the mandatory incorporation notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, summarized corporate purpose, share capital, duration, and the scheduled registration declaration date. Upon payment of the publication fee, the JAL issues the certificate of publication (attestation de parution), the date of which starts the statutory period for creditors' opposition.
required_dossiers: Final signed copy of the articles of association
Identity document of the formation representative
Payment of the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice contains a material error, require the JAL to republish a corrective notice on the next publication day and attach both certificates to the M0 filing; the opposition period runs from the corrected publication date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation application with the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the single national electronic portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (operated by INPI).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Formulaire M0 online, upload the complete dossier in PDF, and digitally sign the application via the portal's authentication system. The Greffe verifies the legal regularity of the Statuts and the annexes, collects the registration fee and the chamber of commerce tax, and issues the RCS registration number and the K-bis extract. Legal personality of the SARL is constituted upon issuance of the K-bis.
required_dossiers: Formulaire M0 completed and electronically signed
Signed articles of association (two originals)
Capital deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
Certificate of publication of the legal notice (JAL)
Declaration of non-conviction of the manager
Proof of the registered office premises (lease, free occupation certificate or utility agreement)
Declaration of the beneficial owner (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs – RBE)
Identity and capacity documents of the legal representative(s)
DPAE pre-hire declaration for the first employee, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for correction (demande de régularisation) or a provisional refusal, submit the rectifying document within 30 days through the portal. Upon final refusal, file a requête en injonction de régulariser before the President of the Commercial Court within 15 days of notification, and thereafter appeal the court's judgment by ordinary appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of K-bis extract and completion of post-registration industrial, sanitary and excise declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for excise duties on beer; Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) for food business declarations; URSSAF for employer registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, retrieve the K-bis extract as the definitive proof of legal existence. Present the K-bis to the depositary bank to release the escrowed capital. Register the company as an employer with URSSAF, file the ICPE declaration or registration with the Prefecture/DREAL if the brewery operates above the exemption threshold, file the food business activity declaration with the DDPP for the cold-chain wholesale and distribution of beer, and complete the DGDDI excise registration (RGA) for duty-suspended beer production and wholesale.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis (register extract of the Commercial and Companies Register)
Manager's resolution authorizing capital release, delivered to the depositary bank
URSSAF employer account creation form and DPAE declarations
DGDDI excise registration application (beer, duty-suspension arrangement)
DDPP food business activity declaration under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004
ICPE declaration or registration package (site plan, technical data sheet, hazardous substances inventory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains errors, request rectification from the Greffe or the issuing chamber; DGDDI excise registration refused or delayed is cured by presenting the provisional receipt of the declaration, and the retailer may operate under the provisional excise identifier. Silence of the DDPP beyond one month is deemed acceptance of the food business declaration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture du département (Préfet), acting through the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) for ICPE permits; Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) for sanitary and food-safety controls; Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for fire safety clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE registration receipt (Récépissé d'enregistrement or de déclaration) under Rubrique 2250 (brasserie – fermented beverages), issued by the Prefect, together with the sanitary activity declaration under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and the DGDDI excise registration (RGA) for beer manufacturing and wholesale distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité Environnementale – Préfet de région, supported by the DREAL Inspection des Installations Classées (Ministry of Ecological Transition).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (enregistrement) or Category D (déclaration) under ICPE Rubrique 2250 for a microbrewery below the authorization threshold of 200,000 hectolitres per year. A full public environmental impact assessment is not mandatory at this scale; the operator files a simplified environmental incidence study (étude d'incidence) and must comply with the standardized ministerial requirements applicable to the declared or registered regime. Reclassification is triggered if production capacity rises or if the site falls within a protected catchment or Natura 2000 area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 5.5–9.5; temperature ≤ 30 °C; suspended solids (MES) ≤ 50 mg/L; BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L; COD ≤ 300 mg/L before discharge to the public sewer, subject to a municipal discharge authorization (autorisation de déversement) and any stricter prefectural limits. Atmospheric: fermentation CO2 routed through a scrubber or recovery system; volatile organic compound (VOC) concentration ≤ 50 mg/m3 with fugitive emissions minimized per the ICPE ministerial order. Waste: spent brewing grain (drêches), yeast residues and diatomaceous earth must be tracked on hazard transfer notes (bordereaux de suivi), sent for recovery as animal feed or compost, and never landfilled without authorization. Noise limits: ≤ 70 dB(A) at the site boundary during daylight operation and ≤ 60 dB(A) at night.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) and the municipal safety commission, including a fire and emergency register, explosion and CO2 detection for fermentation areas, containment for cleaning chemicals, and building conformity for load-bearing capacity, emergency exits, and electrical installation certified by a technical control office (APAVE, Veritas, or SOCOTEC). Occupational clearance: DPAE pre-hire declaration, workplace medical surveillance membership (médecine du travail), mandatory Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), compliance with the Labor Code thresholds for noise (≤ 80 dB(A) daily exposure), lighting, ventilation, ergonomics at the keg-handling station, and registration acknowledgment from the DREETS labor inspector.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SARL obtains SIREN/SIRET automatically upon commercial registry registration; VAT ID (FR + SIREN) assigned upon incorporation or voluntary registration. Foreign entities obtain SIREN via guichet-entreprises.fr and register for TVA if turnover exceeds threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; available options include micro-entreprise regime for SMEs and hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) via PEP platform with API integration and digital stamping for qualifying enterprises.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate on exports of goods outside the EU, requiring proof of dispatch to non-EU destination and non-domestic use in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest and criminal sanctions; retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits upon discovery of non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) acting as the integrated prudential and AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions and payment/e-money institutions. There is no separate foreign exchange control administration in France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is fully integrated into the euro area and maintains unrestricted convertibility for both current and capital account operations under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. No prior exchange-control authorization is required for trade settlements, dividends, shareholder loans, or equity injections. The principal practical hurdle is tax-related rather than FX: outbound profit remittances are subject to a 25% domestic withholding tax, reducible to 0% for qualifying EEA corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or to reduced rates under applicable double tax treaties. Non-EU inbound direct investment may trigger prior screening approval under French FDI regime (Decree 2019-1590) in sensitive sectors, but this is not a convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no fixed repatriation deadline for export proceeds. Exporters may lawfully maintain receivables in foreign currency and manage Forex balances through French bank accounts. For financial statements and corporate income tax purposes, export proceeds must be translated into euro at the applicable Banque de France or accounting reference rate. Reporting obligations are indirect: Intrastat dispatch declarations for intra-EU beer/wine deliveries above the annual threshold, and Single Administrative Documents plus DGDDI customs declarations for third-country exports. The corporate treasury should nevertheless keep export proceeds segregated and traceable to satisfy banking AML and transfer-pricing documentation expectations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. An EU-licensed Electronic Money Institution passported into France can provide remote onboarding, euro IBANs, FX conversion, payment initiation, and virtual accounts; this is workable as a contingency rail. An offshore, non-EEA digital EMI has Low feasibility because it would require an ACPR e-money licence or French branch under Article L.525-6 of the Code monétaire et financier, and French banks will generally reject transfers from non-licensed providers. EMIs cannot hold funds as deposits, cannot grant credit, and are not adequate for capital escrow, commercial letters of credit, or excise duty payment mechanisms. The primary legal constraint is that PSD2 payment services must be provided through an EU-authorised or French-passported institution only.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose an absolute statutory requirement for face-to-face KYC interviews; secure remote video identification may be accepted under ACPR guidance. In practice, however, most tier-one French banks require at least one physical appearance of the SARL gérant at a French branch, particularly where non-resident shareholders or beneficial owners are present. BNP Paribas and Société Générale will normally accept an in-country physical interview plus notarized/legalized corporate documents; remote-only onboarding is feasible only with iris-grade video verification, a French registered office or legal representative, and no political or PEP risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or foreign UBO obscurity in the SARL ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate extract (extrait K-bis), full shareholder register, up-to-date beneficial owner declaration under the French Trust and Beneficial Ownership Register, passports and residence permits of all natural-person shareholders, tax residence certificates from the countries of residence, source of wealth and source of funds statements, notarized contribution certificates, and a corporate structure chart showing the entire ownership chain to ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed SARL with no audited financial history and no French trading footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan for the craft beer distribution undertaking, lease or proof of warehouse and cold-chain facility, French customs and excise registration (Certificat d'accises / DGDDI), distributor letters of intent, supplier agreements with breweries, net worth evidence from the contributing shareholders, personal financial references, and a projected six-month cash-flow statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose or mismatch between declared ISIC 4632 activity and payment traffic.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the statuts, KBIS showing 'commerce de gros de boissons', valid CI number (SIREN/SIRET), DGDDI licence for alcoholic beverage wholesaling, actual invoices and transport documents for hazy IPA kegs, Incoterms contracts, insurance certificates for excise/customs guarantees, and an explanation of anticipated FX flows to and from non-French distributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injection into an intermediation company triggering source-of-funds review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized minutes of the capital increase, depository certificate of funds, bank statements of the investing entity proving prior lawful accumulation, audited financial statements or solicitors' escrow letter, signed shareholder loan agreement if funds come as current account advances, and a sanctions and adverse-media screening report prepared by a regulated third-party provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 for non-euro inbound transfers or a SEPA Credit Transfer in euro, credited to the French beneficiary bank account (BIC/IBAN) of the SARL. The payment MUST include the correct Banque de France payment purpose code to avoid automatic hold: use category C100 for direct investment equity subscription, or an intercompany loan category for a shareholder current-account advance (e.g. compte courant d'associé). The remitting entity must be exactly the same legal person as the shareholder named in the capital increase minutes; third-party payments are unacceptable. Supporting documents should include the French FDI clearance decision, if applicable, the deposit certificate, and a legal cover letter identifying the purpose code, underlying transaction, and ultimate beneficial owner. Funds must be booked to a dedicated capital escrow account before activation of operating accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For distributor payments inside the EEA, execute euro SEPA Credit Transfers (or SEPA Instant for urgent transfers) directly to European IBANs. For outside the EEA, clear trade settlements through SWIFT MT103 with full invoice and customs references; for large keg shipments on documentary terms, use an irrevocable, confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit issued through the French relationship bank. Cold-chain logistics, duty exactions, and DGDDI excise deferments should be handled through the bank's trade finance module, with Incoterms carefully matched to transfer of title. Local direct debit rails can be used for recurring subscriptions from French bars/restaurants, but the primary cross-border rail remains SWIFT/SEPA with MT103 and optional electronic bank document matching.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF executed under a standard treasury line with same-day or T+2 settlement.
Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts with maturities up to 12 months backed by underlying export or import invoices, ideally executed on an ISDA or French bank master agreement.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) but only in currencies without a deliverable euro market and only where the corporate has a demonstrable real exposure; NDFs are not permitted for speculative use.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) used to hedge long-term shareholder loans or acquisition financing, subject to internal hedge documentation.

Purchased European-style FX options (zero-premium collars and vanilla calls/puts) to provide protection without exposing the SARL to margin calls; barrier and exotic options should be avoided for a distribution company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration confirmation (déclaration annuelle de confirmation d'inscription) confirming unchanged RCS data, including beneficial-ownership record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de Paris (via Infogreffe portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March (first quarter of each calendar year, inclusive)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm triggers a Greffe reminder and formal notice; persistent omission is reported to the Procureur de la République, may result in an injunction with coercive daily fine (astreinte) and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS, causing automatic loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the ordinary shareholders' meeting and deposit of the certified annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Infogreffe system; public notice published at BODACC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting to approve the annual accounts within 6 months after financial year-end (extendable only by court order); account deposit with the Greffe within 1 month of approval, i.e. effectively within 7 months of financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted deposit exposes the SARL to a fine of up to EUR 7,500 (legal person) and EUR 1,500 (manager) under Article L123-11-1 Code de commerce; the Commercial Court may order injunctions with coercive daily fines and, upon repeated default, initiate strike-off/radiation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale: Forms 2065-SD and 2052 to 2059-SD, including balance sheet and reconciliation schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via EDI-FCA/EFC e-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December financial year-end, the second working day after 1 May of the following year; for non-calendar year-ends, the last day of the third month following the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed corporate income tax, raised to 10% after a 30-day formal demand (Article 1728 CGI); 40% surcharge if deliberate concealment; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Appointment of a certified statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory where the SARL exceeds two of the three thresholds: total assets exceeding EUR 4 million, net turnover excluding VAT exceeding EUR 8 million, and average headcount exceeding 50 employees; the thresholds are generally measured over the financial year and trigger the audit obligation for the following financial period. Any shareholder holding at least one-third of the capital may petition the Commercial Court for an ad hoc audit appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Accounting Standards (Plan Comptable Général per Regulation ANC 2014-03, as amended), compliant with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; abbreviated/simplified format permitted for micro and small entities under French 'micro' and 'petites entreprises' regimes; IFRS not required for unlisted SARL individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual RCS confirmation statement (due 1 January to 31 March) re-validates that the UBO declaration and registered shareholding data remain unchanged. Any transfer of SARL shares must be recorded in the statutory register of share movements, filed as an RCS modification (Form M) with the Greffe within 30 days of the transfer, and reflected in the updated beneficial-owner declaration; the transfer is also subject to the 3% registration duty payable to DGFiP when formalised. Failure to update the UBO record is punishable by fines up to EUR 3,750 for the SARL and EUR 18,750 for managing officers under Article L561-34-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres et registre des décisions d'associés)
Register of Managers' and Shareholders' Deliberations (registre des procès-verbaux des décisions du gérant et de l'assemblée)
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) and Minute Book of shareholders' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100-3,300 (approx. EUR 1,000-3,000) typical annual fee for professional registered-office domiciliation and corporate secretarial agent services; central Paris location falls at the upper bound
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500-16,500 (approx. EUR 5,000-15,000) typical range for the statutory audit by a registered commissaire aux comptes, scaled to the size and operational complexity of the SARL; reduced fee applicable where micro-entity exemption or simplified audit scope applies

stage_6.entry_description: Legal identification: SIREN, SIRET, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office; APE/NAF code for the principal activity (e.g., 4634Z wholesale of beverages for craft-beer distribution); TVA intracommunity number.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the directing manager (gérant) and ultimate beneficial owners regardless of residence; non-resident shareholders must be declared in the beneficial-owner register (RBE); ensure a French registered office and effective management seat are evidenced.
